title: Regular-sequence divisibility and functions on a two-chart scheme
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative integral domain (a nonzero commutative ring with no zero divisors), and let $s,t\in A$ be nonzero elements forming a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Write $A_s,A_t,A_{st}$ for the localizations obtained by inverting $s,t,st$ respectively [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Let $q:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a scheme morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with an affine open cover $Z=U\cup V$, and specify $A$-algebra identifications $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_Z)=C\subseteq A_s$ and $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)=D\subseteq A_t$. The inclusions are injective unital $A$-algebra maps; the $A$-actions on the section rings are those of $q$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Assume that whenever $c\in C$ and $d\in D$ have equal restrictions on $U\cap V$, their images in $A_{st}$ coincide. Then the coefficient map
$$A\longrightarrow\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$$
is an isomorphism of rings. More precisely, if the chart values of $v\in\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ have images $a/s^r\in A_s$ and $b/t^n\in A_t$ with $r,n\ge1$, there is a unique $e\in A$ with $a=s^re$ and $b=t^ne$, and $v=q^\sharp(e)$.

source.place: Tag 07DV (lemma-regular-sequence-powers); two-chart divisibility and sheaf gluing argument for resolve.tex Tag 0AGS(4), n=0, generalized to an arbitrary two-chart A-scheme

proof.text: Let $v\in\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$, and write its chart images as $a/s^r$ and $b/t^n$. Fraction representatives exist by the definition of localization; replacing $a/s^0$ by $sa/s$ (and similarly for $t$) ensures $r,n\ge1$. The chart sections have equal restrictions, so the hypothesis makes their images equal in $A_{st}$. There $s$ and $t$ have inverses $t/(st)$ and $s/(st)$. Multiplying the equality by $s^rt^n$ gives equality of the images of $t^na$ and $s^rb$. The localization equality criterion gives $(st)^k(t^na-s^rb)=0$ for some $k\ge0$. Since $A$ is a domain and $st\ne0$, cancel $(st)^k$ to obtain $t^na=s^rb$ in $A$.

source.place: Tag 07DV (lemma-regular-sequence-powers), applied to the pair; explicit coefficient calculation for resolve.tex Tag 0AGS (lemma-cohomology-of-blowup), clause (4), n=0

proof.text: Apply the positive-powers theorem with $R=M=A$, the sequence $(s,t)$ and exponents $(r,n)$. It says that $(s^r,t^n)$ is regular. Thus multiplication by $t^n$ on $A/(s^r)$ is injective. Reducing $t^na=s^rb$ modulo $(s^r)$ gives $t^n\bar a=0$, hence $\bar a=0$. Membership in the principal ideal means $a=s^re$ for some $e\in A$. Substitution gives $s^r(t^ne-b)=0$; cancel the nonzero $s^r$ to obtain $b=t^ne$. If also $a=s^re^{\prime}$, cancellation in $s^r(e-e^{\prime})=0$ gives $e=e^{\prime}$.

source.place: Tag 07DV (lemma-regular-sequence-powers), applied to the pair; explicit coefficient calculation for resolve.tex Tag 0AGS (lemma-cohomology-of-blowup), clause (4), n=0

proof.text: View $e$ as a section of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$ using $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal O)=A$. In $A_s$ and $A_t$ the two fraction values equal $e/1$, respectively. Because both chart identifications are injective $A$-algebra maps with the actions induced by $q$, these are exactly the images of $(q^\sharp(e))|_U$ and $(q^\sharp(e))|_V$. Injectivity therefore gives $v|_U=q^\sharp(e)|_U$ and $v|_V=q^\sharp(e)|_V$. The uniqueness clause of the sheaf axiom on $Z=U\cup V$ gives $v=q^\sharp(e)$. This proves surjectivity and the asserted formula for every specified positive-denominator representation.

source.place: Tag 006T (definition-sheaf), uniqueness on the two-open cover; resolve.tex Tag 0AGS(4), n=0, explicit chart argument

proof.text: If $q^\sharp(e)=q^\sharp(e^{\prime})$, restrict to $U$ and use its $A$-algebra embedding into $A_s$. Then $e/1=e^{\prime}/1$ in $A_s$, so $s^k(e-e^{\prime})=0$ for some $k\ge0$. Since $s\ne0$ and $A$ is a domain, $e=e^{\prime}$. Write $f=q^\sharp$ and let $g$ send a global section to its unique coefficient from step 3. We have $f(g(v))=v$, and injectivity gives $g(f(e))=e$. For global sections $v,w$, the identities $f(g(v+w))=v+w=f(g(v)+g(w))$ and $f(g(vw))=vw=f(g(v)g(w))$ imply $g(v+w)=g(v)+g(w)$ and $g(vw)=g(v)g(w)$ by injectivity; likewise $f(g(1))=1=f(1)$ gives $g(1)=1$. Thus $g$ is an inverse ring homomorphism, proving the asserted ring isomorphism.
